title: A Data-Driven Closed-Loop Control Approach to Drive Neural State Transitions for Mechanistic Insight.
evidence_anchors: Methods 'Data', 'Dynamical system reconstruction', and 'Control framework'; Results figures report power-spectrum Hellinger distance, functional-connectivity agreement, 80-step controlled trajectories, target proximity, control energy, and 11 region-restricted controls; Data Availability identifies humml-lab/fmri-control.
reviewer_notes: Planning is demonstrated only in the learned fMRI model. The controls are simulated and not clinical interventions. Test-segment loss is used to select among five initialized models, and there is no external validation, formal calibration, causal treatment claim, or safety test.

title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
evidence_anchors: Preprint Methods define the synthetic 10-ward/200-patient/300-staff hospital, T=7/H=7 prediction, partial surveillance, five-policy branch, common deterministic noise, and constrained optimization; Results report surveillance and distribution-shift stress tests and policy ranking; equation defines ΔB7(a)=B7(baseline)-B7(a).
reviewer_notes: The causal/policy contrast is fully defined inside a known synthetic simulator, hence causal evidence is strong for that simulated data-generating process but does not establish real-hospital effects. The learned predictor is fixed-horizon, not shown consuming its own generated states recursively. Frozen validation is synthetic zero-shot shift.

title: CardamomOT: a mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling
evidence_anchors: BioRxiv API abstract/version record states joint GRN/protein trajectory reconstruction and prediction of unseen perturbations; official CardamomOT README, configs, tests, dataset modules, and results/figure scripts document mechanistic transcription/translation/degradation, Semrau/Kameneva/Schiebinger data, synthetic networks, AUPR/velocity analyses, dropout/time-point noise, and KO/overexpression/stimulus operators.
reviewer_notes: Full PDF/HTML access was blocked by bioRxiv HTTP 1015, so exact sample counts, paper tables, numerical findings, complete baselines, statistical procedures, maximum horizon, and frozen-validation status are NI rather than guessed. Counterfactual language is present, but no explicit population intervention estimand or complete causal identification was found in accessible primary artifacts.

title: DITTO: A Visual Digital Twin for Interventions and Temporal Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Cancer.
evidence_anchors: Accepted manuscript Sections 3-5, quantitative evaluation tables, DITTO workflow/interface figures, two case studies, and Appendix A.2; temporal outputs are shown at 12/24/36/48 months and to 5 years; MC dropout uses at least 20 samples; propensity matching requires at least 5 comparators within a caliper; formative work involved 11 physicians.
reviewer_notes: The accepted manuscript supports retrospective sequential treatment comparison and clinician-facing utility, not prospective planning efficacy. Main text reports 526 patients while Appendix A.2 reports 536=389+147; this discrepancy is retained. Nominal dropout intervals are not empirically calibrated, and no public code, weights, external validation, action-removal test, or hazard test was found.

title: Digital twin brain simulator for real-time consciousness monitoring and virtual intervention using primate electrocorticogram data
evidence_anchors: Methods describe 4 macaques, 20 ECoG channels/10 regions, hierarchical z1/z2/z3 V-RNN, four-fold held-out-animal evaluation, rolling-500-observation/100-update assimilation, and virtual intervention; Results and supplement report power spectra, connectivity, latent clusters, 1-100-step prediction error, and 2,000-step virtual intervention.
reviewer_notes: The held-out animal is evaluated before subsequent assimilation, supporting a frozen population-transfer result, while adapted results are distinguished. Virtual drug action is a latent model perturbation, not administered treatment. Variational uncertainty is not formal calibration; no code, weights, causal estimand, or safety test was reported.

title: Koopman-based linearization of preparatory EEG dynamics in Parkinson's disease during galvanic vestibular stimulation.
evidence_anchors: Methods report 18 PD and 18 control participants, subject-level six-fold splits, three-dimensional Koopman state, 1-15-step m-step prediction, and LQR; Results report horizon-specific NMSE, observed sham/GVS1/GVS2 and medication contrasts, spatial maps, motor correlations, and controlled-versus-uncontrolled LQR trajectories; Code Availability reports a public repository.
reviewer_notes: Observed GVS conditions provide partial causal support for stimulation-associated differences, but the LQR action and steering result remain model simulations without an explicit treatment estimand or real model-directed intervention. There is no external validation, calibrated uncertainty, or stimulation-hazard evaluation.

title: Modelling neural coding in the auditory midbrain with high resolution and accuracy.
evidence_anchors: Methods describe 14 gerbils, high-resolution sound/MUA alignment, 64-dimensional bottleneck, categorical 0-4 event-count decoder, held-out sounds, random 10% validation, leave-one-animal encoder freezing with decoder adaptation, and bootstrap=1,000; Results evaluate RMSE, likelihood, Fano factor, explainable variance, forward masking, and adaptation; official ICNet repository includes code, config, examples, and DNN/model_weights.hdf5.
reviewer_notes: ICNet predicts full response sequences conditional on the complete exogenous sound, so it is action/stimulus-conditioned but not autonomous free-running rollout. Cross-animal evidence requires decoder adaptation and is not frozen external validation. Controlled stimulus manipulations count as action perturbations, but there is no action-agnostic comparator framed for the claimed conditional model.

title: Optimized glycemic control of type 2 diabetes with reinforcement learning: a proof-of-concept trial.
evidence_anchors: Methods report 12,981 inpatients/119,941 patient-days, seven daily periods, transformer patient model, model-based RL, patient-level internal and frozen external-hospital validation, physician review, 20-patient prospective deployment, and NCT05409391; trial Results report 16 patients, glucose reduction from 11.1±3.6 to 8.6±2.4 mmol/L (P<0.01), physician override, and no severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia with ketosis; Data/Code Availability reports RL-DITR and a minimum Zenodo dataset.
reviewer_notes: This is the strongest real closed-loop evidence in the batch, but the clinical trial is a small single-arm before/after feasibility study, not randomized policy comparison. Weighted interval score is uncertainty evaluation but not formal calibration. No action-removal/shuffle or randomized dose perturbation supports action-evidence level 2.

title: Simulating the outcome of amyloid treatments in Alzheimer's disease from imaging and clinical data.
evidence_anchors: Methods define 442 amyloid-positive ADNI participants/2,781 observations, irregular multimodal data, four coupled latent disease components, Gaussian decoders, and intervention simulation; Results figures compare natural history with 50%/100% amyloid lowering over intervention times and long disease-course trajectories; Discussion explicitly bounds conclusions as hypothetical model-based scenarios.
reviewer_notes: The paper defines a clear no-treatment versus dose/timing intervention contrast, but no treated outcomes identify that contrast. Causal evidence is therefore partial: confounding, empirical overlap, and treatment-effect validation are unavailable. Long trajectories are generated, but performance degradation is not reported at multiple rollout horizons. No code, trained parameters, formal calibration, or safety model was found.

title: Towards Causality-Aware Inferring: A Sequential Discriminative Approach for Medical Diagnosis.
evidence_anchors: Methods define MZ (586/142; 66 symptoms/4 diseases) and DX (423/104; 41 symptoms/5 diseases), propensity latent matching, progressive assurance inquiry/diagnosis, Ptrain-to-Pall OOD evaluation, 1/3-symptom inquiry budgets, five-fold analysis, and five seeds; Results include matching/masking ablations, sequential diagnostic success, OOD comparisons, and six-physician blinded evaluation; official CAMAD repository provides code.
reviewer_notes: The closed loop is a short patient-simulator dialogue, not live clinical use. Matching and intervention-inspired masking address two observed inquiry biases but do not specify a causal treatment estimand or complete identification assumptions. Confidence thresholds and limited query budgets are safety-adjacent, not an explicit hazard test. Cross-dataset/OOD evidence is useful but not frozen institutional validation.
